beats.intro: A formula is an equation with several letters, like the area of a rectangle. [[q]]Sometimes you need a different letter on its own. Rewriting the formula gets it there.
beats.area: The area of a rectangle is length times width: A equals l w. [[pic]]A rectangle with area twenty-four square centimeters is six centimeters long. [[q]]How wide is it? [[solve]]Treat w as the unknown. l multiplies w, so divide both sides by l. [[res]]w equals A over l. [[use]]Now plug in: twenty-four over six is four centimeters. [[why]]Rewriting once gives a formula you can reuse for any rectangle.
beats.steps: Rewriting a formula uses the same inverse operations as solving an equation. The other letters simply act like numbers. [[q]]Solve a plus eight b equals c, for a. [[move]]Eight b is added to a, so subtract eight b from both sides. [[res]]a equals c minus eight b. [[q2]]Now solve y equals m x plus b, for x. [[s1]]First subtract b from both sides: y minus b equals m x. [[s2]]Then divide both sides by m. [[res2]]x equals y minus b, all over m.
beats.temp: Here's a formula that turns Fahrenheit into Celsius: C equals five ninths times F minus thirty-two. [[q]]To go the other way, solve for F. [[s1]]Multiply both sides by nine fifths, the reciprocal of five ninths: nine fifths C equals F minus thirty-two. [[s2]]Add thirty-two to both sides. [[res]]F equals nine fifths C plus thirty-two. [[use]]A pleasant day of twenty degrees Celsius: nine fifths of twenty is thirty-six, plus thirty-two is sixty-eight degrees Fahrenheit.
beats.fraction: When the letter you want is in a denominator, clear the fractions first. [[q]]Solve two over x equals five thirds, for x. [[mul]]Multiply both sides by three x, which cancels both denominators. [[res]]That leaves six equals five x, [[div]]so x equals six fifths.

beats.wrap: To rewrite a formula, [[w1]]decide which letter you want on its own, [[w2]]and treat every other letter like a number. [[w3]]Undo operations with inverses, doing the same thing to both sides, until that letter is alone. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
